extracted.intended_audience: authors, illustrators, publishers, librarians, and nominators submitting or evaluating books for the Theodor Seuss Geisel Award
extracted.subtask_description: Terms and criteria for the Theodor Seuss Geisel Award: who is eligible, what counts as a qualifying book for beginning readers (pre-K–grade 2), and the specific literary, artistic, and format qualities the selection committee must consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Award
rubrics_metrics.description: The Theodor Seuss Geisel Award recognizes the author(s) and illustrator(s) of a book for beginning readers who, through their literary and artistic achievements, demonstrate creativity and imagination to engage children in reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This frames the award's evaluative aim: books should specifically engage beginning readers by creative literary and artistic means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the Award (most distinguished contribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: The award shall be given annually to the author and illustrator of the most distinguished contribution to the body of American children’s literature that encourages and supports the beginning reader published in English in the United States during the preceding year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation is comparative across eligible U.S.-published books in English from the preceding year; the winning work should be considered the "most distinguished" contribution that encourages/supports beginning readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and Function for Beginning Readers
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no limitations as to the character of the book considered except that it will be original and function successfully as a book for beginning readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book must be an original work (not merely a reprint/compilation) and must practically work as a beginning-reader book (see detailed criteria on readability, illustrations, pacing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor Book Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Honor Books may be named. These shall be books that are also truly distinguished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honor Books are secondary recognitions that must meet the same high standard of being "truly distinguished."

rubrics_metrics.name: Author/Illustrator Citizenship or Residency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Award is restricted to author(s) and illustrator(s) who are citizens or residents of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only U.S. citizens or U.S. residents as authors/illustrators are eligible for the medal/honor status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility Restricted to Eligible Books Only
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee in its deliberations is to consider only the books eligible for the award, as specified in the terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committees should exclude ineligible items (e.g., reprints, compilations, books not published in the U.S. in English, etc.) when deliberating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-authorship and Posthumous Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: "The 'author(s) and illustrator(s)' may include co-authors and co-illustrators. The author(s) and illustrator(s) may be awarded the medal posthumously."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple creators are permitted and awards can be given posthumously; nomination and attribution should reflect co-creators appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "Distinguished"
rubrics_metrics.description: "Distinguished" is defined as: Marked by distinction: noted for significant achievement; Marked by excellence in quality; Marked by conspicuous excellence or eminence; Individually distinct; Providing a stimulating and successful reading experience for the beginning reader containing the kind of plot, sensibility, and rhythm that can carry a child along from start to finish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives evaluators concrete senses of excellence to look for: overall quality, distinction, and the ability to sustain a beginning reader's engagement via plot, sensibility, and rhythm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original U.S. Publication Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "American children’s literature" means that books originally published in other countries are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only books originally published in the United States are eligible; translations or first publications elsewhere disqualify a title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target Age/Grade Range
rubrics_metrics.description: "Contribution to the body of children’s literature that encourages and supports the beginning reader" indicates the text of a book, which must be directed at readers from pre-K through Grade 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text must be intentionally aimed at beginning readers (pre-K to Grade 2); evaluation should consider developmental appropriateness for that range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and Function of Illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: The book must also contain illustrations, which function as keys or clues to the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations are required and must actively support comprehension (serve as keys/clues), not merely be decorative; they should help beginning readers decode/understand the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted Forms of Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee shall consider all forms of writing—fiction, non-fiction, and poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility spans genres and forms; evaluators should apply criteria across fiction, non-fiction, and poetry tailored to beginning-reader needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprints and Compilations Ineligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Reprints and compilations are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books that are reissued material or collections of previously published pieces are excluded from consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject Matter Must Motivate Reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter must be intriguing enough to motivate the child to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should assess whether the topic/content is engaging and motivating specifically for beginning readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter Structure (flexibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The book may or may not include short "chapters".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure may vary; inclusion of short chapters is permitted but not required. The key is whether structure supports beginning-reader engagement and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocabulary Introduction Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: New words should be added slowly enough to make learning them a positive experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how new vocabulary is introduced—pace new word exposure so it supports learning rather than overwhelming the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Repetition for Retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Words should be repeated to ensure knowledge retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repetition of words/phrases is a positive technique for beginning-reader books; assess how repetition aids retention and understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence Simplicity and Directness
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentences must be simple and straightforward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language should be age-appropriate in syntax and clarity; complex or convoluted sentence structures are discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page Length Constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a minimum of 24 pages. Books may not be longer than 96 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical/page-length limits define format expectations for beginning-reader books; ensure submissions fall within 24–96 pages inclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations Must Demonstrate the Story
rubrics_metrics.description: The illustrations must demonstrate the story being told.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations should advance or clarify the narrative—showing action, emotion, or context—not merely decorate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successful Reading Experience from Start to Finish
rubrics_metrics.description: The book creates a successful reading experience, from start to finish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the work's overall cohesiveness and its capacity to sustain comprehension and enjoyment across the entire book for beginning readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page-to-Page Plot Advancement and Page-turning Dynamic
rubrics_metrics.description: The plot advances from one page to the next and creates a "page-turning" dynamic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate pacing and suspense/curiosity that encourage the reader to continue; each page should propel the story forward in a way accessible to beginning readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and Frequency of Award (procedural)
rubrics_metrics.description: One Theodor Seuss Geisel Award for one book will be announced in January of each year during the American Library Association Midwinter Meeting ... If a suitable candidate is not found for any given year, the award will not be presented that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural constraint: one medal annually (or none if no suitable candidate); timing tied to ALA Midwinter Meeting announcement schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Jury (procedural)
rubrics_metrics.description: The President of the Association for Library Service to Children ... will appoint the committee to administer the award. Membership shall be one chair and six members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee composition is defined; evaluators are appointed by the ALSC President and should follow committee procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for Nominations (procedural)
rubrics_metrics.description: The deadline for award entries is December 31. The committee will consider books for the award up to and including this date. The dates of the Midwinter Meeting may affect the date the nominations are due, but will be specified on a yearly basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations must be submitted by December 31 (subject to yearly scheduling adjustments). Committees consider books published up to that date.
